Root cause is Cluster E2: Publication mismatch with an earlier Incorrect source acquisition (the chosen publish target is not the canonical source of truth for this product). The actual gap is that nothing automatically re-triggers regeneration when the override data changes, so a genuinely correct, working hard gate can sit dirty indefinitely with no forcing function. Root cause is Cluster E3 (closest available label: Publication mismatch, though this stretches the given taxonomy -- flagged honestly as a scheduling/orchestration gap, not a pure data-mismatch one). Fix: when platform_canonical_overrides.yaml/aspose_com_targets.json changes a validated_via target for an already-generated product, automatically queue it for regeneration, or at minimum surface it in the next session-start/backlog sweep. title: Fix two 100%-reproducible bugs in the shared candidate-verification marker writer
determination: _write_candidate_verification_marker (readme_refresh_run.py:584-594) has two confirmed-universal defects. (1) Line 588 hashes text.encode('utf-8') where text comes from candidate_path.read_text(encoding='utf-8') (line 1964), whose default universal-newline translation strips CRLF -- the recorded hash never matches the file's real on-disk bytes on any Windows-run refresh. (2) verified_by_run_id is null on 31/31 products (100%, two independent sweeps) -- but direct code read of all 3 call sites shows this is NOT because the field is never threaded: ingest_candidate (line 1973) and recheck (line 3087) both pass a real run_id. title: Enforce the human-approval gate in code, not just by convention

A naming convention cannot fix an authority problem. CORRECTED MECHANISM: relocate the actual point of human control from a string an agent can supply to an action only a human, using their own real GitHub credentials, can perform -- require every push to open a real PR (already how the system works, gh pr create) and gate data/readme_published_state.json's 'published' status EXCLUSIVELY on a real, externally-observed PR merge event (via gh api, checking the merging actor's GitHub identity is not the pipeline's own bot/token identity), never on the pipeline's own approve/push call succeeding. This composes directly with RC-publication-ledger-reconciliation (which already needs to read PR/merge history). Not perfect -- a human could still merge without real scrutiny -- but it removes the specific failure mode this card names (an agent completing its own approval loop end-to-end), which the original identity-marker idea did not.

title: Promote content-addressed identity to the default disposition backbone across all 4 unit-level ledgers (content/structural/code-example/badge)
determination: Foundational item from phase6b section I, the 'sharpest finding' of the production-hardening design pass, that was never turned into its own executable RC-* card. extract_old_readme_content_units (and its 3 sibling extractors: structural s%04d, code-example c%04d, badge b%04d) assigns a stable, ORDER-based unit_id -- the code's own MT056 comment (readme_refresh_checks.py:5350-5366) already states this positional scheme is 'the confirmed root cause of the R-07 disposition-drift regression class.' The fix already exists in this codebase for a narrower purpose: compute_block_fingerprints implements content-addressed (sha256) identity at ##-section granularity for the opt-in surgical-scope workflow. This card extends that same hashing idea down to unit granularity for the 4 ledgers that actually carry the defect (Cluster A, 11/36 rows, the largest cluster in the audit). ROLLOUT (revised from a one-shot batch migration after adversarial critique found real risk in that approach): additive dual-key -- add a content_hash field alongside the existing positional unit_id on every NEW disposition entry going forward; consuming checks read content_hash when present, fall back to unit_id when absent; re-key each product's EXISTING ledgers lazily, the next time that product is genuinely touched, never as a portfolio-wide batch pass. COLLISION HANDLING: salt the hash with the unit's position within its OWNING SECTION (stable unless the section itself is restructured) rather than its position in the whole document (unstable under any earlier edit) -- near-duplicate units are a real, known phenomenon in this corpus (see check_content_unit_probable_duplicate), so a bare content hash alone is not sufficient identity at this granularity. CANARIES, split by purpose: pdf/net and slides/java prove the mechanism works on a clean baseline; email/cpp is the dedicated NEGATIVE-path test (its content-dispositions.json was built against a known-corrupted 'old readme' baseline per Phase 4 row 26 -- re-keying it should correctly route everything to an UNRESOLVED_NEEDS_HUMAN_REDISPOSITION bucket, not silently accept a false-clean re-key).
